identification.summary: BRONZE SPIRAL is the Secureworks Counter Threat Unit name for the actor Secureworks earlier called SPIRAL, which Secureworks linked to deployment of the SUPERNOVA web shell on an internet-facing SolarWinds Orion server in late 2020[S2]. Secureworks assessed the group appears to be based in China, and reporting did not say whether it is state-affiliated or criminal[S2]. Secureworks said the SUPERNOVA intrusion is unrelated to the broader SolarWinds supply-chain compromise[S2], and CISA likewise assessed the SUPERNOVA actor in its own incident as separate from the supply-chain APT [S5].
identification.firstObserved: 2020 (earliest Secureworks-linked intrusion; reported as August 2020 by secondary coverage) [S6]
identification.notes: Name mapping: the SPIRAL (2021 Secureworks blog) and BRONZE SPIRAL naming is taken from the Secureworks title and search summaries; the Sophos threat-profile page for BRONZE SPIRAL could not be fetched, so its content is not cited here. Do not merge with the CISA-described Pulse Secure/Orion intrusion: CISA did not name an actor, and no source here states it is the same cluster as SPIRAL [S5]. Do not merge with the unrelated 2026 'Spirals' ransomware family or with 2021 ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus campaigns, which these sources do not tie to SPIRAL.

attribution.confidence: Secureworks said characteristics of the intrusions suggest the group is based in China; the sources do not state a sponsor or government affiliation[S6]. No government attribution found.
attribution.basis: Secureworks CTU tied a second intrusion at the same client, using SUPERNOVA in late 2020, to earlier 2020 activity by the same actor, and cited characteristics that suggest a China base[S6].

targeting.notes: Secureworks described intrusions at one client network involving a ManageEngine ServiceDesk server (reconnaissance and credential theft) and an internet-facing SolarWinds server; the client's sector and country are not given in the available coverage [S6].

capabilities.summary: The SUPERNOVA web shell is a .NET implant hidden in a modified Orion module, app_web_logoimagehandler.ashx.b6031896.dll, that receives remote code and runs it in memory without writing artifacts to disk [S3]. The DLL was unsigned, unlike the SUNBURST DLL of the supply-chain operation [S3]. Secureworks said the exploited flaw was CVE-2020-10148, an Orion API authentication bypass, used before the 23 Dec 2020 SolarWinds patch[S2]. CISA's separate incident analysis described SUPERNOVA as a webshell that lets an operator inject C# code, placed directly on Orion hosts rather than delivered by a trojanized update [S5].

campaigns.name: ManageEngine ServiceDesk intrusion
campaigns.summary: Secureworks linked an earlier 2020 intrusion at the same client, involving a ManageEngine ServiceDesk server, reconnaissance and credential theft, to the SPIRAL actor [S6].

campaigns.name: SUPERNOVA deployment on SolarWinds Orion
campaigns.summary: Secureworks CTU observed the actor exploit an internet-facing SolarWinds server to deploy the SUPERNOVA web shell in late 2020[S2][S6]. Dark Reading coverage reports the actor then moved to a domain controller for credentials and to a server with sensitive data [S8].

campaigns.name: Public disclosure of SUPERNOVA
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 and GuidePoint analyzed the trojanized Orion DLL; Unit 42 questioned association with the SolarStorm (SUNBURST) actors because the DLL was unsigned [S3].

campaigns.name: Secureworks links SUPERNOVA to SPIRAL
campaigns.summary: Secureworks published 'SUPERNOVA Web Shell Deployment Linked to SPIRAL Threat Group', assessing the activity as likely China-based and unrelated to the supply-chain compromise[S2].

diamond.adversary: SPIRAL / BRONZE SPIRAL, assessed by Secureworks as likely China-based; affiliation unknown[S6].
diamond.capability: SUPERNOVA in-memory .NET web shell and exploitation of CVE-2020-10148[S3].
diamond.victim: One client network with ManageEngine ServiceDesk and SolarWinds Orion servers; identity not stated in available coverage [S6].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing SolarWinds Orion and ManageEngine ServiceDesk servers[S6].

provenance.importedSummary: In December 2020, the IT management software provider SolarWinds announced that an unidentified threat actor had exploited a vulnerability in their Orion Platform software to deploy a web shell dubbed SUPERNOVA. CTU researchers track the operators of the SUPERNOVA web shell as BRONZE SPIRAL and assess with low confidence that the group is of Chinese origin. SUPERNOVA was likely deployed through exploitation of CVE-2020-10148, and CTU researchers observed post-exploitation reconnaissance commands roughly 30 minutes before the web shell was deployed. This may have been indicative of the threat actor conducting scan-and-exploit activity and then triaging for victims of particular interest, before deploying SUPERNOVA and attempting to dump credentials and move laterally. BRONZE SPIRAL has been associated with previous intrusions involving the targeting of ManageEngine servers, maintenance of long-term access to periodically harvest credentials and exfiltrate data, and espionage or theft of intellectual property. The threat group makes extensive use of native system tools and 'living off the land' techniques.
